Root task: spd-b39-user-opened-inspector-shape-successor. Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-charter.md (read via git show origin/main — the primary checkout runs commits behind and returns confident-empty greps). This Paper is the wave's living story; every later phase appends to it.
The wish, verbatim

THIS CYCLE: STUDIO SPACE-PRIORITY DESK — the user-opened inspector still crushes the reading surface. Fix the highest-value inspector/desk defects with protective tests and name the shortest path to seal.
Where the epic stands (14 waves in)

The founding defect — a user-opened inspector crushing the reading column — is SOLVED IN SHAPE and LIVE on the deployed build (D190). Wide (1280+) docks the inspector IN FLOW via the Tier-2 ladder (display_state/5, #4922). Narrow/phone is a SUMMONED full-panel destination with dimming ABOLISHED and a Tier-3 return grammar (#4923/#5014/#5015). Keyboard Escape + focus-in + focus-return is PAID (#5086). Round-trip fidelity returns the reading column BIT-IDENTICAL at 27/27 cells on the deployed build (D182). The scoped compound selector is LAW; the paper-reader crush was the founding defect and it is dead in every CLEAN bucket.
But one reachable state still dims LIVE PROSE on origin/main — and it is the named SEAL-BLOCKER 2. This wave pays it.
The defect, precisely — the compound secondary_doc state

The scrim is an ::after overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.55), position absolute, anchored to .editor-panel) that lives inside the @container panel (max-width: 860px) block in root.html.heex. It exists to signal 'the inspector is ON TOP'. It only paints when the content panel is <= 860px.

In a CLEAN standard bucket (viewport 1024-1279, no secondary pane), the inspector user-opened leaves panel = 976px — ABOVE 860 — so the @container generator never fires and no scrim paints. The clean standard bucket is NOT crushed.

The breach is the COMPOUND state (D175/D187/D192). Open a Tasks doc, use the secondary picker (spd-w5 fix, 99 candidates live) to pin a secondary pane, collapse the root to a 44px strip, then navigate the primary to a Paper. Scope.select/2 is push_patch — the LiveView never remounts — and secondary_doc SURVIVES the navigation because NEITHER clear_paper_view/1 (paper.ex:740) NOR setup_paper_view/2 (paper.ex:600/662) clears it on origin/main. Now .editor-panel = 1024 - 44 - 360 = 620px < 860, the generator fires, and the ::after scrim paints OVER LIVE PROSE: measured mean luminance over 310,000 pixels drops 240.493 -> 175.104 (delta 65.389 darker). That is the exact D127 defect — the reader's column dimmed — reached through an orthogonal affordance, and it is LIVE on main.
The direction — kill the last reachable crush, invariant-first

The ROOT CAUSE is behavioral, not cosmetic: a stale secondary_doc persisting across navigation. The scrim is the downstream symptom. So the wave attacks the cause AND hardens the symptom, each fix MUTATION-PROVEN able to fail:

FIX 1 (the root cause, in-fence, provable without the operator) — shared/paper.ex clears secondary_doc on BOTH navigation legs: clear_paper_view/1 (paper -> non-paper) and setup_paper_view/2 (paper -> paper). With the stale secondary pane gone, the standard panel never drops below 860 via this path and the scrim never gets a chance to paint. Wave 14 pinned the CURRENT persistence with a test; this wave FLIPS it — the test now asserts secondary_doc == nil after each leg, with paper_doc proving the nav path actually ran (non-vacuity).

FIX 2 (the invariant, root.html.heex — SOLE OWNER this wave, verified uncontended) — the standard bucket is aligned to the rule the epic already ruled: LIVE PROSE IS NEVER DIMMED BY A SUMMONED INSPECTOR (D127). Wide docks in-flow (no scrim); narrow abolishes dimming; the standard bucket follows. This is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH for any other path that shrinks the panel, guarded by a File.read! CSS-reader test mutation-proven against a synthetic sabotaged selector (the D193 pattern). Crucially this is APPLYING a settled rule, not making a new shape decision — it does not touch the D127-ordering trap (no mode is exempted after seeing an unfavourable table; dimming live prose is simply always wrong).

The finished experience: on the deployed build there is NO reachable state — clean or compound, any bucket — in which a user-opened inspector dims or crushes the reading column. That closes the founding defect for real, not just in the clean case.
The direction debate

RIVAL A (WINNER) — Pay the live breach. Behavioral secondary_doc clear as the spine (root cause, in-fence, no operator, no shape decision), plus the root.html.heex scrim invariant as a co-slice (uncontended, defense-in-depth). Both mutation-proven. Names residue: the bracketed run (operator), the ledger reconcile (lead).

RIVAL B — Shape-first: rule the standard-bucket inspector shape in the charter (dock vs destination vs exempt) and rebuild the inspector for standard. REJECTED: docking arithmetic already loses (a 300px dock at 1024 yields 34ch, WORSE than the overlay), the founding defect is unreachable in clean standard (panel 976), and D190 already ruled this epic 'convergence, not design'. A full shape rebuild is over-engineering a bug a nav-clear fixes, and it risks freeze contention and stranding.

RIVAL C — Test-hardening only (a wave-14 redux): keep guarding, defer the fix to the lead post-freeze. REJECTED: the breach stays LIVE and the wish says FIX, not merely PROVE. Adding tests around a known-broken behaviour banks no user value.
WHY A WON: it is the only candidate that removes the live crush this wave, at low risk, without a design decision the arithmetic already forecloses, on files the lead verified uncontended.

SHARPEST ATTACK ON A: 'The behavioral clear may not be the ONLY path to a shrunk standard panel — if some standard width (764, 700) already puts panel <= 860 with the inspector open and NO secondary doc, then clearing secondary_doc does not kill the scrim and a shape ruling is unavoidable.' ABSORPTION: survey questions 5 and 11 enumerate every reachable standard-bucket state where panel <= 860, with and without a secondary doc. If clean standard never crosses 860, FIX 1 is sufficient and FIX 2 is pure hardening. If it does, FIX 2's invariant (never dim live prose) handles it WITHOUT a shape rebuild — abolishing dimming of prose is a settled rule, not a new mode exemption.
Tentative slice shape (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

S1 — shared/paper.ex: clear secondary_doc in clear_paper_view/1 AND setup_paper_view/2; author/flip the mutation-proven Elixir test (secondary_doc == nil after both legs; non-vacuity via paper_doc). Files: shared/paper.ex + new test. In-fence, no root.html.heex, no operator.

S2 — root.html.heex: harden the invariant that live prose is never dimmed in the standard bucket; author a File.read! CSS-reader guard mutation-proven with a synthetic sabotaged selector. SOLE OWNER of root.html.heex (D16 satisfied — exactly one writer). Files: root.html.heex + new guard test.

The scrim is an ::after overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.55), position absolute, anchored to .editor-panel) that lives inside the @container panel (max-width: 860px) block in root.html.heex. It exists to signal 'the inspector is ON TOP'. It only paints when the content panel is <= 860px.

The wish, verbatim

THIS CYCLE: STUDIO SPACE-PRIORITY DESK — the user-opened inspector still crushes the reading surface. Fix the highest-value inspector/desk defects with protective tests and name the shortest path to seal.

Where the epic stands (14 waves in)

The founding defect — a user-opened inspector crushing the reading column — is SOLVED IN SHAPE and LIVE on the deployed build (D190). Wide (1280+) docks the inspector IN FLOW via the Tier-2 ladder (display_state/5, #4922). Round-trip fidelity returns the reading column BIT-IDENTICAL at 27/27 cells on the deployed build (D182). The scoped compound selector is LAW; the paper-reader crush was the founding defect and it is dead in every CLEAN bucket.

But one reachable state still dims LIVE PROSE on origin/main — and it is the named SEAL-BLOCKER 2. This wave pays it.

The defect, precisely — the compound secondary_doc state

The scrim is an ::after overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.55), position absolute, anchored to .editor-panel) that lives inside the @container panel (max-width: 860px) block in root.html.heex. It exists to signal 'the inspector is ON TOP'. It only paints when the content panel is <= 860px.

In a CLEAN standard bucket (viewport 1024-1279, no secondary pane), the inspector user-opened leaves panel = 976px — ABOVE 860 — so the @container generator never fires and no scrim paints. The clean standard bucket is NOT crushed.

The breach is the COMPOUND state (D175/D187/D192). Open a Tasks doc, use the secondary picker (spd-w5 fix, 99 candidates live) to pin a secondary pane, collapse the root to a 44px strip, then navigate the primary to a Paper. Scope.select/2 is push_patch — the LiveView never remounts — and secondary_doc SURVIVES the navigation because NEITHER clear_paper_view/1 (paper.ex:740) NOR setup_paper_view/2 (paper.ex:600/662) clears it on origin/main. Now .editor-panel = 1024 - 44 - 360 = 620px < 860, the generator fires, and the ::after scrim paints OVER LIVE PROSE: measured mean luminance over 310,000 pixels drops 240.493 -> 175.104 (delta 65.389 darker). That is the exact D127 defect — the reader's column dimmed — reached through an orthogonal affordance, and it is LIVE on main.

The direction — kill the last reachable crush, invariant-first

The ROOT CAUSE is behavioral, not cosmetic: a stale secondary_doc persisting across navigation. The scrim is the downstream symptom. So the wave attacks the cause AND hardens the symptom, each fix MUTATION-PROVEN able to fail:

FIX 1 (the root cause, in-fence, provable without the operator) — shared/paper.ex clears secondary_doc on BOTH navigation legs: clear_paper_view/1 (paper -> non-paper) and setup_paper_view/2 (paper -> paper). Wave 14 pinned the CURRENT persistence with a test; this wave FLIPS it — the test now asserts secondary_doc == nil after each leg, with paper_doc proving the nav path actually ran (non-vacuity).

FIX 2 (the invariant, root.html.heex — SOLE OWNER this wave, verified uncontended) — the standard bucket is aligned to the rule the epic already ruled: LIVE PROSE IS NEVER DIMMED BY A SUMMONED INSPECTOR (D127). Wide docks in-flow (no scrim); narrow abolishes dimming; the standard bucket follows. This is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH for any other path that shrinks the panel, guarded by a File.read! CSS-reader test mutation-proven against a synthetic sabotaged selector (the D193 pattern). Crucially this is APPLYING a settled rule, not making a new shape decision — it does not touch the D127-ordering trap (no mode is exempted after seeing an unfavourable table; dimming live prose is simply always wrong).

The finished experience: on the deployed build there is NO reachable state — clean or compound, any bucket — in which a user-opened inspector dims or crushes the reading column. That closes the founding defect for real, not just in the clean case.

Genuinely strong: the wave does exactly what the wish asked — kill the highest-value reachable inspector/desk crush with protective tests and name the seal path — and nothing more.
